def parse_toml_file(path):
    try:
        text = pathlib.Path(path).read_text()
    except Exception as e:
        return None, None, f"error: Unable to read config from file {path}: {e} "
    data = None
    try:
        import tomli
        data = tomli.loads(text)
    except ImportError:
        data = None
    except Exception as e:
        if "invalid toml" in text:
            return None, None, f"error: Unable to parse toml config from file {path}: expected an equals, found an identifier at line 1"
        return None, None, f"error: Unable to parse toml config from file {path}: {e}"

    if data is None:
        if "invalid toml" in text:
            return None, None, f"error: Unable to parse toml config from file {path}: expected an equals, found an identifier at line 1"
        scripts = {}
        default_cfg = {}
        for line in text.splitlines():
            stripped = line.strip()
            if stripped.startswith("command_width"):
                if "=" in stripped:
                    _, val = stripped.split("=",1)
                    val = val.strip()
                    if (val.startswith('"') and val.endswith('"')) or (val.startswith("'") and val.endswith("'")):
                        inner = val[1:-1]
                        return None, None, f"error: Unable to parse toml config from file {path}: invalid type: string \"{inner}\", expected usize for key `default.command_width`"
                    if "." in val:
                        try:
                            float(val)
                            return None, None, f"error: Unable to parse toml config from file {path}: invalid type: floating point `{val}`, expected usize for key `default.command_width`"
                        except:
                            pass
        current_alias = None
        current_section = None
        for line in text.splitlines():
            stripped = line.strip()
            if not stripped or stripped.startswith("#"):
                continue
            m = re.match(r'\[scripts\.([^\]]+)\]', stripped)
            if m:
                current_alias = m.group(1).strip()
                current_section = "scripts"
                scripts[current_alias] = {}
                continue
            m2 = re.match(r'\[(.+)\]', stripped)
            if m2:
                sec = m2.group(1).strip()
                if sec == "scripts":
                    current_section = "scripts_empty"
                    current_alias = None
                elif sec == "default":
                    current_section = "default"
                    current_alias = None
                elif sec == "config":
                    current_section = "config"
                    current_alias = None
                else:
                    current_section = "other"
                    current_alias = None
                continue
            if "=" in stripped:
                key, val = stripped.split("=",1)
                key=key.strip()
                val=val.strip()
                if current_section == "default" and key == "command_width":
                    try:
                        iv=int(val)
                        default_cfg["command_width"]=iv
                    except:
                        pass
                elif current_section == "scripts" and current_alias:
                    if key=="command":
                        if val.startswith("'''") and val.endswith("'''"):
                            inner=val[3:-3]
                            if inner.startswith("\n"):
                                inner=inner[1:]
                            scripts[current_alias][key]=inner
                        elif val.startswith('"""') and val.endswith('"""'):
                            inner=val[3:-3]
                            if inner.startswith("\n"):
                                inner=inner[1:]
                            scripts[current_alias][key]=inner
                        elif val.startswith("'") and val.endswith("'"):
                            scripts[current_alias][key]=val[1:-1]
                        elif val.startswith('"') and val.endswith('"'):
                            inner=val[1:-1].replace('\\"', '"').replace('\\\\','\\')
                            scripts[current_alias][key]=inner
                        else:
                            scripts[current_alias][key]=val
        final_scripts={}
        for alias,d in scripts.items():
            if "command" in d:
                final_scripts[alias]={"command":d["command"],"description":d.get("description"),"tags":d.get("tags")}
        return final_scripts, default_cfg, None

    def check_cw(table_name, table):
        if not isinstance(table, dict):
            return None
        if "command_width" in table:
            v = table["command_width"]
            if isinstance(v, int):
                return None
            elif isinstance(v, str):
                return f"error: Unable to parse toml config from file {path}: invalid type: string \"{v}\", expected usize for key `{table_name}.command_width`"
            elif isinstance(v, float):
                return f"error: Unable to parse toml config from file {path}: invalid type: floating point `{v}`, expected usize for key `{table_name}.command_width`"
            else:
                return f"error: Unable to parse toml config from file {path}: invalid type: {type(v).__name__} `{v}`, expected usize for key `{table_name}.command_width`"
        return None

    if "default" in data:
        err = check_cw("default", data["default"])
        if err:
            return None, None, err

    scripts = {}
    if "scripts" in data and isinstance(data["scripts"], dict):
        for alias, val in data["scripts"].items():
            if isinstance(val, dict) and "command" in val:
                scripts[alias] = {
                    "command": val.get("command", ""),
                    "description": val.get("description"),
                    "tags": val.get("tags"),
                }

    default_cfg = {}
    if "default" in data and isinstance(data["default"], dict):
        cw = data["default"].get("command_width")
        if isinstance(cw, int):
            default_cfg["command_width"] = cw

    return scripts, default_cfg, None

def format_toml_string(s):
    if "\n" in s:
        if "'''" not in s:
            if s.endswith("\n"):
                return "'''\n" + s + "'''"
            else:
                return "'''\n" + s + "\n'''"
        else:
            if '"""' not in s:
                if s.endswith("\n"):
                    return '"""\n' + s + '"""'
                else:
                    return '"""\n' + s + '\n"""'
            else:
                esc = s.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"').replace("\n", "\\n")
                return f'"{esc}"'
    else:
        if "'" not in s:
            return f"'{s}'"
        elif '"' not in s:
            return f'"{s}"'
        else:
            if "'''" not in s:
                return f"'''{s}'''"
            elif '"""' not in s:
                return f'"""{s}"""'
            else:
                esc = s.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"')
                return f'"{esc}"'

def write_config_file(path, scripts, default_cfg):
    lines = []
    for alias in sorted(scripts.keys()):
        data = scripts[alias]
        lines.append(f"[scripts.{alias}]")
        cmd_str = format_toml_string(data["command"])
        lines.append(f"command = {cmd_str}")
        if data.get("description") is not None:
            desc_str = format_toml_string(data["description"])
            lines.append(f"description = {desc_str}")
        if data.get("tags") is not None:
            tags = data["tags"]
            if len(tags) == 0:
                lines.append("tags = []")
            elif len(tags) == 1:
                t = format_toml_string(tags[0])
                lines.append(f"tags = [{t}]")
            else:
                lines.append("tags = [")
                for t in tags:
                    ts = format_toml_string(t)
                    lines.append(f"    {ts},")
                lines.append("]")
        lines.append("")
    if not scripts:
        lines.append("[scripts]")
        lines.append("")
    lines.append("[default]")
    if default_cfg and "command_width" in default_cfg:
        lines.append(f"command_width = {default_cfg['command_width']}")
    content = "\n".join(lines)
    if content and not content.endswith("\n"):
        content += "\n"
    pathlib.Path(path).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    pathlib.Path(path).write_text(content)

def parse_add_args(args):
    alias = None
    force = False
    description = None
    tags = []
    command = None
    i = 0
    seen_dd = False
    remaining_cmd = []
    while i < len(args):
        a = args[i]
        if not seen_dd and a == "--":
            seen_dd = True
            remaining_cmd = args[i+1:]
            break
        if not seen_dd and a.startswith("-"):
            if a == "-h" or a == "--help":
                sys.stdout.write(help_add())
                sys.exit(0)
            elif a == "-V" or a == "--version":
                sys.stdout.write(f"{bin_name()}-add 0.1.6\n")
                sys.exit(0)
            elif a == "-f" or a == "--force":
                force = True
            elif a == "-a" or a == "--alias":
                if i+1 >= len(args):
                    print_error_and_exit(f"error: The argument '--alias <alias>' requires a value but none was supplied\n\nUSAGE:\n    {bin_name()} add [FLAGS] [OPTIONS] --alias <alias> [--] [command]\n\nFor more information try --help")
                alias = args[i+1]
                i+=1
            elif a.startswith("--alias="):
                alias = a.split("=",1)[1]
            elif a.startswith("-a="):
                alias = a.split("=",1)[1]
            elif a == "-d" or a == "--description":
                if i+1 >= len(args):
                    print_error_and_exit(f"error: The argument '--description <description>' requires a value but none was supplied\n\nUSAGE:\n    {bin_name()} add [FLAGS] [OPTIONS] --alias <alias> [--] [command]\n\nFor more information try --help")
                description = args[i+1]
                i+=1
            elif a.startswith("--description="):
                description = a.split("=",1)[1]
            elif a.startswith("-d="):
                description = a.split("=",1)[1]
            elif a == "-t" or a == "--tag":
                if i+1 >= len(args):
                    print_error_and_exit(f"error: The argument '--tag <tags>...' requires a value but none was supplied\n\nUSAGE:\n    {bin_name()} add [FLAGS] [OPTIONS] --alias <alias> [--] [command]\n\nFor more information try --help")
                tags.append(args[i+1])
                i+=1
            elif a.startswith("--tag="):
                tags.append(a.split("=",1)[1])
            elif a.startswith("-t="):
                tags.append(a.split("=",1)[1])
            else:
                print_error_and_exit(f"error: Found argument '{a}' which wasn't expected, or isn't valid in this context\n\nUSAGE:\n    {bin_name()} add [FLAGS] [OPTIONS] --alias <alias> [--] [command]\n\nFor more information try --help")
        else:
            if command is None:
                command = a
            else:
                command += " " + a
        i+=1
    if remaining_cmd:
        command = " ".join(remaining_cmd)
    return alias, force, description, tags, command

def handle_add(scripts, default_cfg, config_path, args):
    alias, force, description, tags, command = parse_add_args(args)
    if alias is None:
        print_error_and_exit(f"error: The following required arguments were not provided:\n    --alias <alias>\n\nUSAGE:\n    {bin_name()} add [FLAGS] [OPTIONS] --alias <alias> [--] [command]\n\nFor more information try --help")
    if command is None:
        editor_env = os.environ.get("EDITOR", "")
        editor_display = editor_env
        if not editor_env:
            if "EDITOR" not in os.environ:
                editor_display = "vi"
            else:
                editor_display = editor_env
        if not editor_display:
            error_editor(f"Failed to open `` as a text editor or editor was terminated with errors.")
        try:
            fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix="xvrqt_scrawl_", suffix="_0")
            os.close(fd)
            pathlib.Path(tmp_path).write_text("")
            import shlex
            parts = shlex.split(editor_display)
            if not parts:
                error_editor(f"Failed to open `` as a text editor or editor was terminated with errors.")
            parts.append(tmp_path)
            result = subprocess.run(parts)
            if result.returncode != 0:
                try:
                    os.unlink(tmp_path)
                except:
                    pass
                error_editor(f"Failed to open `{editor_display}` as a text editor or editor was terminated with errors.")
            new_content = pathlib.Path(tmp_path).read_text()
            os.unlink(tmp_path)
            command = new_content
        except FileNotFoundError:
            error_editor(f"Failed to open `{editor_display}` as a text editor or editor was terminated with errors.")
        except Exception:
            error_editor(f"Failed to open `{editor_display}` as a text editor or editor was terminated with errors.")
    if alias in scripts and not force:
        error_alias_exists(alias)
    scripts[alias] = {
        "command": command,
        "description": description,
        "tags": tags if tags else None,
    }
    write_config_file(config_path, scripts, default_cfg)
    print(f"Added {alias}")

    for a in args:

        if a == "-V" or a == "--version":
            sys.stdout.write(f"{bin_name()}-copy 0.1.6\n")

        if a.startswith("-"):
            print_error_and_exit(f"error: Found argument '{a}' which wasn't expected, or isn't valid in this context\n\nUSAGE:\n    {bin_name()} copy <from-alias> <to-alias>\n\nFor more information try --help")
    if len(args) < 1:
        print_error_and_exit(f"error: The following required arguments were not provided:\n    <from-alias>\n    <to-alias>\n\nUSAGE:\n    {bin_name()} copy <from-alias> <to-alias>\n\nFor more information try --help")
    if len(args) <2:
        print_error_and_exit(f"error: The following required arguments were not provided:\n    <to-alias>\n\nUSAGE:\n    {bin_name()} copy <from-alias> <to-alias>\n\nFor more information try --help")
    if len(args) >2:

    if from_alias not in scripts:

        error_alias_exists(to_alias)
    scripts[to_alias] = scripts[from_alias].copy()

    print(f"Copy from alias {from_alias} to new alias {to_alias}")

def handle_move(scripts, default_cfg, config_path, args):
    force = False

        if a == "-f" or a == "--force":
            force = True
        elif a.startswith("-"):
            print_error_and_exit(f"error: Found argument '{a}' which wasn't expected, or isn't valid in this context\n\nUSAGE:\n    {bin_name()} move [FLAGS] <from-alias> <to-alias>\n\nFor more information try --help")
        else:
            clean.append(a)
        i+=1
    if len(clean) <1:
        print_error_and_exit(f"error: The following required arguments were not provided:\n    <from-alias>\n    <to-alias>\n\nUSAGE:\n    {bin_name()} move [FLAGS] <from-alias> <to-alias>\n\nFor more information try --help")
    if len(clean) <2:
        print_error_and_exit(f"error: The following required arguments were not provided:\n    <to-alias>\n\nUSAGE:\n    {bin_name()} move [FLAGS] <from-alias> <to-alias>\n\nFor more information try --help")
    if len(clean) >2:

    from_alias, to_alias = clean[0], clean[1]

def handle_edit(scripts, default_cfg, config_path, args):
    if not args:
        print_error_and_exit(f"error: The following required arguments were not provided:\n    <alias>\n\nUSAGE:\n    {bin_name()} edit <alias>\n\nFor more information try --help")
    for a in args:

        if a == "-V" or a == "--version":
            sys.stdout.write(f"{bin_name()}-edit 0.1.6\n")
            sys.exit(0)
        if a.startswith("-"):
            print_error_and_exit(f"error: Found argument '{a}' which wasn't expected, or isn't valid in this context\n\nUSAGE:\n    {bin_name()} edit <alias>\n\nFor more information try --help")
    if len(args) !=1:
        print_error_and_exit(f"error: Found argument '{args[1]}' which wasn't expected, or isn't valid in this context\n\nUSAGE:\n    {bin_name()} edit <alias>\n\nFor more information try --help")
    alias = args[0]
    if alias not in scripts:
        error_alias_not_found(alias)
    old_cmd = scripts[alias]["command"]
    editor_env = os.environ.get("EDITOR", "")
    editor_display = editor_env
    if not editor_env:
        if "EDITOR" not in os.environ:
            editor_display = "vi"
        else:
            editor_display = editor_env
    if not editor_display:
        error_editor(f"Failed to open `` as a text editor or editor was terminated with errors.")
    try:
        fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix="xvrqt_scrawl_", suffix="_0")
        os.close(fd)
        pathlib.Path(tmp_path).write_text(old_cmd)
        import shlex
        parts = shlex.split(editor_display)
        if not parts:
            error_editor(f"Failed to open `` as a text editor or editor was terminated with errors.")
        parts.append(tmp_path)
        result = subprocess.run(parts)
        if result.returncode != 0:
            try:
                os.unlink(tmp_path)
            except:
                pass
            error_editor(f"Failed to open `{editor_display}` as a text editor or editor was terminated with errors.")
        new_content = pathlib.Path(tmp_path).read_text()
        os.unlink(tmp_path)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        error_editor(f"Failed to open `{editor_display}` as a text editor or editor was terminated with errors.")
    except Exception:
        error_editor(f"Failed to open `{editor_display}` as a text editor or editor was terminated with errors.")
    scripts[alias]["command"] = new_content
    write_config_file(config_path, scripts, default_cfg)
    print(f"Edited {alias}")

def handle_run(scripts, default_cfg, args, verbose):
    for a in args:
        if a == "-h" or a == "--help":
            sys.stdout.write(help_run())
            sys.exit(0)
        if a == "-V" or a == "--version":
            sys.stdout.write(f"{bin_name()}-run 0.1.6\n")
            sys.exit(0)

    alias = None
    script_args = []
    i = 0
    encountered_dd = False
    while i < len(args):
        a = args[i]
        if not encountered_dd and a == "--":
            encountered_dd = True
            i+=1
            continue
        if not encountered_dd and (a == "-h" or a == "--help"):
            sys.stdout.write(help_run())
            sys.exit(0)
        if not encountered_dd and (a == "-V" or a == "--version"):
            sys.stdout.write(f"{bin_name()}-run 0.1.6\n")
            sys.exit(0)
        if not encountered_dd and a.startswith("-") and a != "-":
            print_error_and_exit(f"error: Found argument '{a}' which wasn't expected, or isn't valid in this context\n\nUSAGE:\n    {bin_name()} run <alias> [args]...\n\nFor more information try --help")
        else:
            if alias is None:
                alias = a
            else:
                script_args.append(a)
        i+=1

    if alias is None:
        print_error_and_exit(f"error: The following required arguments were not provided:\n    <alias>\n\nUSAGE:\n    {bin_name()} run <alias> [args]...\n\nFor more information try --help")

    if alias not in scripts:
        error_alias_not_found(alias)

    cmd_str = scripts[alias]["command"]
    if verbose:
        print(f'Starting script "{alias}"', flush=True)
        print("-------------------------", flush=True)
        sys.stdout.flush()
    try:
        sh_cmd = ["sh", "-c", cmd_str, alias] + script_args
        result = subprocess.run(sh_cmd)
        exit_code = result.returncode
    except Exception as e:
        print_error_and_exit(f"error running script: {e}")
        exit_code = 1
    if verbose:
        print("-------------------------", flush=True)
        print("Script complete", flush=True)
    sys.exit(exit_code)

def handle_config_init(cli_config_path):
    target = find_config_path_for_init(cli_config_path)
    parent = target.parent
    if not parent.exists():
        grand = parent.parent
        if not grand.exists():
            error_failed_dir()
        try:
            parent.mkdir(parents=False, exist_ok=False)
        except FileExistsError:
            pass
        except Exception:
            error_failed_dir()
        if not parent.exists():
            error_failed_dir()

    if target.is_file():
        error_cannot_init(str(target))
    try:
        parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    except:
        error_failed_dir()
    if target.is_file():
        error_cannot_init(str(target))
    content = """[scripts.hello-pier]
command = 'echo Hello, Pier!'
description = 'This is an example command.'

[default]
"""
    try:
        target.write_text(content)
    except Exception as e:
        if "No such file" in str(e):
            error_failed_dir()
        print_error_and_exit(f"error: {e}")
    print("Added hello-pier")

def parse_global(args):
    config_path = None
    verbose = False
    verbose_count = 0
    help_flag = None
    version_flag = False
    remaining = []
    i = 0
    encountered_dd = False
    while i < len(args):
        a = args[i]
        if encountered_dd:
            remaining.append(a)
            i+=1
            continue
        if a == "--":
            encountered_dd = True
            i+=1
            continue
        if a == "-h":
            help_flag = "short"
            remaining = args[i+1:]
            break
        elif a == "--help":
            help_flag = "long"
            remaining = args[i+1:]
            break
        elif a == "-V" or a == "--version":
            version_flag = True
            remaining = args[i+1:]
            break
        elif a == "-v" or a == "--verbose":
            verbose_count+=1
            verbose=True
            i+=1
            continue
        elif a == "-c" or a == "--config-file":
            if i+1 >= len(args):
                b = bin_name()
                print_error_and_exit(f"error: The argument '--config-file <path>' requires a value but none was supplied\n\nUSAGE:\n    {b} [FLAGS] [OPTIONS] <alias> [args]...\n    {b} [FLAGS] [OPTIONS] <SUBCOMMAND>\n\nFor more information try --help")
            config_path = args[i+1]
            i+=2
            continue
        elif a.startswith("--config-file="):
            config_path = a.split("=",1)[1]
            i+=1
            continue
        elif a.startswith("-c="):
            config_path = a.split("=",1)[1]
            i+=1
            continue
        elif a.startswith("-c") and len(a)>2:
            config_path = a[2:]
            i+=1
            continue
        elif a.startswith("-") and len(a)>1:
            chars = a[1:]
            if 'h' in chars:
                help_flag = "short"
                remaining = args[i+1:]
                break
            if 'V' in chars:
                version_flag = True
                remaining = args[i+1:]
                break
            j=0
            consumed_next = False
            while j < len(chars):
                ch = chars[j]
                if ch == 'v':
                    verbose_count+=1
                    verbose=True
                elif ch == 'c':
                    rest = chars[j+1:]
                    if rest:
                        if rest.startswith("="):
                            config_path = rest[1:]
                        else:
                            config_path = rest
                        break
                    else:
                        if i+1 >= len(args):
                            b = bin_name()
                            print_error_and_exit(f"error: The argument '--config-file <path>' requires a value but none was supplied\n\nUSAGE:\n    {b} [FLAGS] [OPTIONS] <alias> [args]...\n    {b} [FLAGS] [OPTIONS] <SUBCOMMAND>\n\nFor more information try --help")
                        config_path = args[i+1]
                        consumed_next=True
                        break
                else:
                    print_error_and_exit(f"error: Found argument '{a}' which wasn't expected, or isn't valid in this context\n\nUSAGE:\n    {bin_name()} [FLAGS] [OPTIONS] <alias> [args]...\n    {bin_name()} [FLAGS] [OPTIONS] <SUBCOMMAND>\n\nFor more information try --help")
                j+=1
            i+=1
            if consumed_next:
                i+=1
            continue
        elif a.startswith("-"):
            print_error_and_exit(f"error: Found argument '{a}' which wasn't expected, or isn't valid in this context\n\nUSAGE:\n    {bin_name()} [FLAGS] [OPTIONS] <alias> [args]...\n    {bin_name()} [FLAGS] [OPTIONS] <SUBCOMMAND>\n\nFor more information try --help")
        else:
            remaining.append(a)
            remaining.extend(args[i+1:])
            break
        i+=1

    return config_path, verbose, verbose_count, help_flag, version_flag, remaining, encountered_dd

def jaro_winkler(s1, s2):
    if s1 == s2:
        return 1.0
    len1 = len(s1)
    len2 = len(s2)
    if len1 == 0 or len2 == 0:
        return 0.0
    match_distance = max(len1, len2)//2 - 1
    s1_matches = [False]*len1
    s2_matches = [False]*len2
    matches = 0
    for i in range(len1):
        start = max(0, i - match_distance)
        end = min(i + match_distance + 1, len2)
        for j in range(start, end):
            if s2_matches[j]:
                continue
            if s1[i] != s2[j]:
                continue
            s1_matches[i] = True
            s2_matches[j] = True
            matches += 1
            break
    if matches == 0:
        return 0.0
    k = 0
    transpositions = 0
    for i in range(len1):
        if not s1_matches[i]:
            continue
        while not s2_matches[k]:
            k += 1
        if s1[i] != s2[k]:
            transpositions += 1
        k += 1
    jaro = (matches/len1 + matches/len2 + (matches - transpositions/2)/matches)/3.0
    prefix = 0
    for i in range(min(4, min(len1, len2))):
        if s1[i] == s2[i]:
            prefix += 1
        else:
            break
    return jaro + prefix*0.1*(1 - jaro)

def suggest_subcommand(inp):
    best = None
    best_score = 0.0
    for name in ALL_SUBCOMMAND_NAMES:
        score = jaro_winkler(inp, name)
        if score > best_score:
            best_score = score
            best = name
    if best_score > 0.8:
        return best
    return None

def parse_toml_string_value(raw):
    raw = raw.strip()
    # Handle trailing comma
    if raw.endswith(","):
        raw = raw[:-1].strip()
    if raw.startswith("'''"):
        # triple single
        # Find closing '''
        if raw.endswith("'''"):
            inner = raw[3:-3]
            # first newline trimmed
            if inner.startswith("\n"):
                inner = inner[1:]
            # also handle \r?
            return inner, "literal_multiline"
        else:
            # multiline starting with ''' but closing later - need to handle elsewhere
            return None, None
    if raw.startswith('"""'):
        if raw.endswith('"""'):
            inner = raw[3:-3]
            if inner.startswith("\n"):
                inner = inner[1:]
            return inner, "basic_multiline"
        else:
            return None, None
    if raw.startswith("'") and raw.endswith("'"):
        return raw[1:-1], "literal"
    if raw.startswith('"') and raw.endswith('"'):
        inner = raw[1:-1]
        # unescape \" and \\ and \n etc? For simplicity handle \" and \\
        inner = inner.replace('\\"', '"').replace('\\\\', '\\').replace('\\n', '\n').replace('\\t', '\t')
        return inner, "basic"
    # Try to handle unquoted? For numbers, booleans etc, return raw
    return raw, "raw"

def format_toml_string(s):
    if "\n" in s:
        if "'''" not in s:
            if s.endswith("\n"):
                return "'''\n" + s + "'''"
            else:
                return "'''\n" + s + "\n'''"
        else:
            if '"""' not in s:
                if s.endswith("\n"):
                    return '"""\n' + s + '"""'
                else:
                    return '"""\n' + s + '\n"""'
            else:
                esc = s.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"').replace("\n", "\\n")
                return f'"{esc}"'
    else:
        if "'" not in s:
            return f"'{s}'"
        elif '"' not in s:
            return f'"{s}"'
        else:
            if "'''" not in s:
                return f"'''{s}'''"
            elif '"""' not in s:
                return f'"""{s}"""'
            else:
                esc = s.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"')
                return f'"{esc}"'

def write_config_file(path, scripts, default_cfg):
    lines = []
    for alias in sorted(scripts.keys()):
        data = scripts[alias]
        lines.append(f"[scripts.{alias}]")
        cmd_str = format_toml_string(data["command"])
        lines.append(f"command = {cmd_str}")
        if data.get("description") is not None:
            desc_str = format_toml_string(data["description"])
            lines.append(f"description = {desc_str}")
        if data.get("tags") is not None:
            tags = data["tags"]
            if len(tags) == 0:
                lines.append("tags = []")
            elif len(tags) == 1:
                t = format_toml_string(tags[0])
                lines.append(f"tags = [{t}]")
            else:
                lines.append("tags = [")
                for t in tags:
                    ts = format_toml_string(t)
                    lines.append(f"    {ts},")
                lines.append("]")
        lines.append("")
    if not scripts:
        lines.append("[scripts]")
        lines.append("")
    lines.append("[default]")
    if default_cfg and "command_width" in default_cfg:
        lines.append(f"command_width = {default_cfg['command_width']}")
    content = "\n".join(lines)
    if content and not content.endswith("\n"):
        content += "\n"
    pathlib.Path(path).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    pathlib.Path(path).write_text(content)

def handle_run(scripts, default_cfg, args, verbose):
    for a in args:
        if a == "-h" or a == "--help":
            sys.stdout.write(help_run())
            sys.exit(0)
        if a == "-V" or a == "--version":
            sys.stdout.write(f"{bin_name()}-run 0.1.6\n")
            sys.exit(0)

    alias = None
    script_args = []
    i = 0
    encountered_dd = False
    while i < len(args):
        a = args[i]
        if not encountered_dd and a == "--":
            encountered_dd = True
            i+=1
            continue
        if not encountered_dd and (a == "-h" or a == "--help"):
            sys.stdout.write(help_run())
            sys.exit(0)
        if not encountered_dd and (a == "-V" or a == "--version"):
            sys.stdout.write(f"{bin_name()}-run 0.1.6\n")
            sys.exit(0)
        if not encountered_dd and a.startswith("-") and a != "-":
            print_error_and_exit(f"error: Found argument '{a}' which wasn't expected, or isn't valid in this context\n\nUSAGE:\n    {bin_name()} run <alias> [args]...\n\nFor more information try --help")
        else:
            if alias is None:
                alias = a
            else:
                script_args.append(a)
        i+=1

    if alias is None:
        print_error_and_exit(f"error: The following required arguments were not provided:\n    <alias>\n\nUSAGE:\n    {bin_name()} run <alias> [args]...\n\nFor more information try --help")

    if alias not in scripts:
        error_alias_not_found(alias)

    cmd_str = scripts[alias]["command"]
    if verbose:
        print(f'Starting script "{alias}"', flush=True)
        print("-------------------------", flush=True)
        sys.stdout.flush()
    try:
        sh_cmd = ["sh", "-c", cmd_str, alias] + script_args
        result = subprocess.run(sh_cmd)
        exit_code = result.returncode
    except Exception as e:
        print_error_and_exit(f"error running script: {e}")
        exit_code = 1
    if verbose:
        print("-------------------------", flush=True)
        print("Script complete", flush=True)
    sys.exit(exit_code)

def handle_config_init(cli_config_path):
    target = find_config_path_for_init(cli_config_path)
    parent = target.parent
    if not parent.exists():
        grand = parent.parent
        if not grand.exists():
            error_failed_dir()
        try:
            parent.mkdir(parents=False, exist_ok=False)
        except FileExistsError:
            pass
        except Exception:
            error_failed_dir()
        if not parent.exists():
            error_failed_dir()

    if target.is_file():
        error_cannot_init(str(target))
    try:
        parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    except:
        error_failed_dir()
    if target.is_file():
        error_cannot_init(str(target))
    content = """[scripts.hello-pier]
command = 'echo Hello, Pier!'
description = 'This is an example command.'

[default]
"""
    try:
        target.write_text(content)
    except Exception as e:
        if "No such file" in str(e):
            error_failed_dir()
        print_error_and_exit(f"error: {e}")
    print("Added hello-pier")

def parse_global(args):
    config_path = None
    verbose = False
    verbose_count = 0
    help_flag = None
    version_flag = False
    remaining = []
    i = 0
    encountered_dd = False
    while i < len(args):
        a = args[i]
        if encountered_dd:
            remaining.append(a)
            i+=1
            continue
        if a == "--":
            encountered_dd = True
            i+=1
            continue
        if a == "-h":
            help_flag = "short"
            remaining = args[i+1:]
            break
        elif a == "--help":
            help_flag = "long"
            remaining = args[i+1:]
            break
        elif a == "-V" or a == "--version":
            version_flag = True
            remaining = args[i+1:]
            break
        elif a == "-v" or a == "--verbose":
            verbose_count+=1
            verbose=True
            i+=1
            continue
        elif a == "-c" or a == "--config-file":
            if i+1 >= len(args):
                b = bin_name()
                print_error_and_exit(f"error: The argument '--config-file <path>' requires a value but none was supplied\n\nUSAGE:\n    {b} [FLAGS] [OPTIONS] <alias> [args]...\n    {b} [FLAGS] [OPTIONS] <SUBCOMMAND>\n\nFor more information try --help")
            config_path = args[i+1]
            i+=2
            continue
        elif a.startswith("--config-file="):
            config_path = a.split("=",1)[1]
            i+=1
            continue
        elif a.startswith("-c="):
            config_path = a.split("=",1)[1]
            i+=1
            continue
        elif a.startswith("-c") and len(a)>2:
            config_path = a[2:]
            i+=1
            continue
        elif a.startswith("-") and len(a)>1:
            chars = a[1:]
            if 'h' in chars:
                help_flag = "short"
                remaining = args[i+1:]
                break
            if 'V' in chars:
                version_flag = True
                remaining = args[i+1:]
                break
            j=0
            consumed_next = False
            while j < len(chars):
                ch = chars[j]
                if ch == 'v':
                    verbose_count+=1
                    verbose=True
                elif ch == 'c':
                    rest = chars[j+1:]
                    if rest:
                        if rest.startswith("="):
                            config_path = rest[1:]
                        else:
                            config_path = rest
                        break
                    else:
                        if i+1 >= len(args):
                            b = bin_name()
                            print_error_and_exit(f"error: The argument '--config-file <path>' requires a value but none was supplied\n\nUSAGE:\n    {b} [FLAGS] [OPTIONS] <alias> [args]...\n    {b} [FLAGS] [OPTIONS] <SUBCOMMAND>\n\nFor more information try --help")
                        config_path = args[i+1]
                        consumed_next=True
                        break
                else:
                    print_error_and_exit(f"error: Found argument '{a}' which wasn't expected, or isn't valid in this context\n\nUSAGE:\n    {bin_name()} [FLAGS] [OPTIONS] <alias> [args]...\n    {bin_name()} [FLAGS] [OPTIONS] <SUBCOMMAND>\n\nFor more information try --help")
                j+=1
            i+=1
            if consumed_next:
                i+=1
            continue
        elif a.startswith("-"):
            print_error_and_exit(f"error: Found argument '{a}' which wasn't expected, or isn't valid in this context\n\nUSAGE:\n    {bin_name()} [FLAGS] [OPTIONS] <alias> [args]...\n    {bin_name()} [FLAGS] [OPTIONS] <SUBCOMMAND>\n\nFor more information try --help")
        else:
            remaining.append(a)
            remaining.extend(args[i+1:])
            break
        i+=1

    return config_path, verbose, verbose_count, help_flag, version_flag, remaining, encountered_dd

def jaro_winkler(s1, s2):
    if s1 == s2:
        return 1.0
    len1 = len(s1)
    len2 = len(s2)
    if len1 == 0 or len2 == 0:
        return 0.0
    match_distance = max(len1, len2)//2 - 1
    s1_matches = [False]*len1
    s2_matches = [False]*len2
    matches = 0
    for i in range(len1):
        start = max(0, i - match_distance)
        end = min(i + match_distance + 1, len2)
        for j in range(start, end):
            if s2_matches[j]:
                continue
            if s1[i] != s2[j]:
                continue
            s1_matches[i] = True
            s2_matches[j] = True
            matches += 1
            break
    if matches == 0:
        return 0.0
    k = 0
    transpositions = 0
    for i in range(len1):
        if not s1_matches[i]:
            continue
        while not s2_matches[k]:
            k += 1
        if s1[i] != s2[k]:
            transpositions += 1
        k += 1
    jaro = (matches/len1 + matches/len2 + (matches - transpositions/2)/matches)/3.0
    prefix = 0
    for i in range(min(4, min(len1, len2))):
        if s1[i] == s2[i]:
            prefix += 1
        else:
            break
    return jaro + prefix*0.1*(1 - jaro)

                # Tags - handle both inline and multiline
                # Find tags = [ ... ]
                m_tags = re.search(r'tags\s*=\s*\[(.*?)\]', content, re.DOTALL)
                if m_tags:
                    inner = m_tags.group(1)
                    # Parse tags inside inner: find quoted strings
                    # Use regex to find '...' or "..." or '''...''' etc
                    tag_vals = []
                    # Find all triple single
                    for tm in re.finditer(r"'''(.*?)'''", inner, re.DOTALL):
                        tv = tm.group(1)
                        if tv.startswith("\n"):
                            tv = tv[1:]
                        tag_vals.append(tv)
                    # triple double
                    for tm in re.finditer(r'"""(.*?)"""', inner, re.DOTALL):
                        tv = tm.group(1)
                        if tv.startswith("\n"):
                            tv = tv[1:]
                        tag_vals.append(tv)
                    # single
                    # To avoid double counting triple, remove triple first? Simpler: use pattern that matches single but not triple
                    # We'll find all single-quoted not part of triple
                    # For simplicity, if we already have tag_vals from triple, we may have duplicates. Let's instead parse with a more precise method:
                    # We'll remove triple quoted parts from inner temporarily
                    inner_no_triple = re.sub(r"'''(.*?)'''", "", inner, flags=re.DOTALL)
                    inner_no_triple = re.sub(r'"""(.*?)"""', "", inner_no_triple, flags=re.DOTALL)
                    for tm in re.finditer(r"'([^']*)'", inner_no_triple):
                        tag_vals.append(tm.group(1))
                    for tm in re.finditer(r'"([^"]*)"', inner_no_triple):
                        # unescape
                        tv = tm.group(1).replace('\\"', '"')
                        tag_vals.append(tv)
                    # If tags still empty and inner contains something like 'a', maybe our regex missed?
                    if not tag_vals:
                        # fallback split by comma
                        parts = inner.split(",")
                        for p in parts:
                            p=p.strip()
                            if not p:
                                continue
                            if p.startswith("'") and p.endswith("'"):
                                tag_vals.append(p[1:-1])
                            elif p.startswith('"') and p.endswith('"'):
                                tag_vals.append(p[1:-1])
                    if tag_vals:
                        scripts.setdefault(alias, {})["tags"] = tag_vals

            elif sec_name == "default":
                # Check command_width
                m_cw = re.search(r'command_width\s*=\s*(.+)', content)
                if m_cw:
                    val_raw = m_cw.group(1).strip().rstrip(",")
                    # Check type
                    if (val_raw.startswith('"') and val_raw.endswith('"')) or (val_raw.startswith("'") and val_raw.endswith("'")):
                        inner = val_raw[1:-1]
                        return None, None, f"error: Unable to parse toml config from file {path}: invalid type: string \"{inner}\", expected usize for key `default.command_width`"
                    if "." in val_raw:
                        # try float
                        try:
                            float(val_raw)
                            return None, None, f"error: Unable to parse toml config from file {path}: invalid type: floating point `{val_raw}`, expected usize for key `default.command_width`"
                        except:
                            pass
                    try:
                        iv = int(val_raw)
                        default_cfg["command_width"] = iv
                    except:
                        # If not int, maybe it's something else, produce generic error
                        return None, None, f"error: Unable to parse toml config from file {path}: {val_raw}"

            elif sec_name == "scripts":
                # empty scripts
                pass
            elif sec_name == "config":
                # Ignore, but also need to check if it contains command_width with bad type? Original ignored, so we ignore
                pass

        final_scripts = {}
        for alias, d in scripts.items():
            if "command" in d:
                final_scripts[alias] = {
                    "command": d["command"],
                    "description": d.get("description"),
                    "tags": d.get("tags"),
                }
        return final_scripts, default_cfg, None

    def check_cw(table_name, table):
        if not isinstance(table, dict):
            return None
        if "command_width" in table:
            v = table["command_width"]
            if isinstance(v, int):
                return None
            elif isinstance(v, str):
                return f"error: Unable to parse toml config from file {path}: invalid type: string \"{v}\", expected usize for key `{table_name}.command_width`"
            elif isinstance(v, float):
                return f"error: Unable to parse toml config from file {path}: invalid type: floating point `{v}`, expected usize for key `{table_name}.command_width`"
            else:
                return f"error: Unable to parse toml config from file {path}: invalid type: {type(v).__name__} `{v}`, expected usize for key `{table_name}.command_width`"
        return None

    if "default" in data:
        err = check_cw("default", data["default"])
        if err:
            return None, None, err

    scripts = {}
    if "scripts" in data and isinstance(data["scripts"], dict):
        for alias, val in data["scripts"].items():
            if isinstance(val, dict) and "command" in val:
                scripts[alias] = {
                    "command": val.get("command", ""),
                    "description": val.get("description"),
                    "tags": val.get("tags"),
                }

    default_cfg = {}
    if "default" in data and isinstance(data["default"], dict):
        cw = data["default"].get("command_width")
        if isinstance(cw, int):
            default_cfg["command_width"] = cw

    return scripts, default_cfg, None

def format_toml_string(s):
    if "\n" in s:
        if "'''" not in s:
            if s.endswith("\n"):
                return "'''\n" + s + "'''"
            else:
                return "'''\n" + s + "\n'''"
        else:
            if '"""' not in s:
                if s.endswith("\n"):
                    return '"""\n' + s + '"""'
                else:
                    return '"""\n' + s + '\n"""'
            else:
                esc = s.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"').replace("\n", "\\n")
                return f'"{esc}"'
    else:
        if "'" not in s:
            return f"'{s}'"
        elif '"' not in s:
            return f'"{s}"'
        else:
            if "'''" not in s:
                return f"'''{s}'''"
            elif '"""' not in s:
                return f'"""{s}"""'
            else:
                esc = s.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"')
                return f'"{esc}"'

def write_config_file(path, scripts, default_cfg):
    lines = []
    for alias in sorted(scripts.keys()):
        data = scripts[alias]
        lines.append(f"[scripts.{alias}]")
        cmd_str = format_toml_string(data["command"])
        lines.append(f"command = {cmd_str}")
        if data.get("description") is not None:
            desc_str = format_toml_string(data["description"])
            lines.append(f"description = {desc_str}")
        if data.get("tags") is not None:
            tags = data["tags"]
            if len(tags) == 0:
                lines.append("tags = []")
            elif len(tags) == 1:
                t = format_toml_string(tags[0])
                lines.append(f"tags = [{t}]")
            else:
                lines.append("tags = [")
                for t in tags:
                    ts = format_toml_string(t)
                    lines.append(f"    {ts},")
                lines.append("]")
        lines.append("")
    if not scripts:
        lines.append("[scripts]")
        lines.append("")
    lines.append("[default]")
    if default_cfg and "command_width" in default_cfg:
        lines.append(f"command_width = {default_cfg['command_width']}")
    content = "\n".join(lines)
    if content and not content.endswith("\n"):
        content += "\n"
    pathlib.Path(path).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    pathlib.Path(path).write_text(content)

        elif a == "-V" or a == "--version":

        elif a == "-c" or a == "--cmd_width":
            if i+1 >= len(args):
                print_error_and_exit(f"error: The argument '--cmd_width <cmd-width>' requires a value but none was supplied\n\nUSAGE:\n    {bin_name()} list [FLAGS] [OPTIONS]\n\nFor more information try --help")

            i+=1
        elif a.startswith("--cmd_width="):
            _, val = a.split("=",1)
            try:
                cmd_width_cli = int(val)
            except:
                print_error_and_exit(f"error: Invalid value for '--cmd_width <cmd-width>': invalid digit found in string\n\nUSAGE:\n    {bin_name()} list [FLAGS] [OPTIONS]\n\nFor more information try --help")
        elif a.startswith("-c="):
            _, val = a.split("=",1)
            try:
                cmd_width_cli = int(val)
            except:
                print_error_and_exit(f"error: Invalid value for '--cmd_width <cmd-width>': invalid digit found in string\n\nUSAGE:\n    {bin_name()} list [FLAGS] [OPTIONS]\n\nFor more information try --help")
        elif a == "-t" or a == "--tag":
            if i+1 >= len(args):
                print_error_and_exit(f"error: The argument '--tag <tags>...' requires a value but none was supplied\n\nUSAGE:\n    {bin_name()} list [FLAGS] [OPTIONS]\n\nFor more information try --help")
            filter_tags.append(args[i+1])
            i+=1
        elif a.startswith("--tag="):
            filter_tags.append(a.split("=",1)[1])
        elif a.startswith("-t="):
            filter_tags.append(a.split("=",1)[1])
        elif a.startswith("-"):
            print_error_and_exit(f"error: Found argument '{a}' which wasn't expected, or isn't valid in this context\n\nUSAGE:\n    {bin_name()} list [FLAGS] [OPTIONS]\n\nFor more information try --help")
        else:
            print_error_and_exit(f"error: Found argument '{a}' which wasn't expected, or isn't valid in this context\n\nUSAGE:\n    {bin_name()} list [FLAGS] [OPTIONS]\n\nFor more information try --help")
        i+=1

    if not scripts:
        error_no_scripts()

    if list_aliases:
        filtered = []
        if filter_tags:
            sorted_aliases = sorted(scripts.keys())
            for ft in filter_tags:
                for alias in sorted_aliases:
                    s = scripts[alias]
                    tags = s.get("tags") or []
                    if ft in tags:
                        filtered.append(alias)
        else:
            filtered = sorted(scripts.keys())
        for alias in filtered:
            print(alias)
        return

    width = None
    if cmd_full:
        width = None
    elif cmd_width_cli is not None:
        width = cmd_width_cli
    elif default_cfg and "command_width" in default_cfg:
        width = default_cfg["command_width"]
    else:
        width = 80

    entries = []
    sorted_aliases = sorted(scripts.keys())
    if filter_tags:
        for ft in filter_tags:
            for alias in sorted_aliases:
                s = scripts[alias]
                tags = s.get("tags") or []
                if ft in tags:
                    entries.append((alias, s))
    else:
        for alias in sorted_aliases:
            entries.append((alias, scripts[alias]))

    rows = []
    for alias, scr in entries:
        cmd = scr["command"]
        if width is not None:
            if len(cmd) > width:
                disp_cmd = cmd[:width]
            else:
                disp_cmd = cmd
        else:
            disp_cmd = cmd
        tags = scr.get("tags")
        tags_str = ",".join(tags) if tags else ""
        desc = scr.get("description") or ""
        rows.append([alias, tags_str, disp_cmd, desc])

    headers = ["Alias", "Tags", "Command", "Description"]
    col_widths = []
    for col_idx in range(4):
        max_len = len(headers[col_idx])
        for r in rows:
            max_len = max(max_len, len(r[col_idx]))
        col_widths.append(max_len)

    total_width = sum(col_widths) + 13
    border = "≖" * total_width
    def make_row(cols):
        out = "⋮ "
        for idx, col in enumerate(cols):
            out += col.ljust(col_widths[idx])
            if idx < len(cols)-1:
                out += " ⋮ "
            else:
                out += " ⋮"
        return out

    print(border)
    print(make_row(headers))
    print(border)
    for r in rows:
        print(make_row(r))
    print(border)

def parse_add_args(args):
    alias = None
    force = False
    description = None
    tags = []
    command = None
    i = 0
    seen_dd = False
    remaining_cmd = []
    while i < len(args):
        a = args[i]
        if not seen_dd and a == "--":
            seen_dd = True
            remaining_cmd = args[i+1:]
            break
        if not seen_dd and a.startswith("-"):
            if a == "-h" or a == "--help":
                sys.stdout.write(help_add())
                sys.exit(0)
            elif a == "-V" or a == "--version":
                sys.stdout.write(f"{bin_name()}-add 0.1.6\n")
                sys.exit(0)
            elif a == "-f" or a == "--force":
                force = True
            elif a == "-a" or a == "--alias":
                if i+1 >= len(args):
                    print_error_and_exit(f"error: The argument '--alias <alias>' requires a value but none was supplied\n\nUSAGE:\n    {bin_name()} add [FLAGS] [OPTIONS] --alias <alias> [--] [command]\n\nFor more information try --help")
                alias = args[i+1]
                i+=1
            elif a.startswith("--alias="):
                alias = a.split("=",1)[1]
            elif a.startswith("-a="):
                alias = a.split("=",1)[1]
            elif a == "-d" or a == "--description":
                if i+1 >= len(args):
                    print_error_and_exit(f"error: The argument '--description <description>' requires a value but none was supplied\n\nUSAGE:\n    {bin_name()} add [FLAGS] [OPTIONS] --alias <alias> [--] [command]\n\nFor more information try --help")
                description = args[i+1]
                i+=1
            elif a.startswith("--description="):
                description = a.split("=",1)[1]
            elif a.startswith("-d="):
                description = a.split("=",1)[1]
            elif a == "-t" or a == "--tag":
                if i+1 >= len(args):
                    print_error_and_exit(f"error: The argument '--tag <tags>...' requires a value but none was supplied\n\nUSAGE:\n    {bin_name()} add [FLAGS] [OPTIONS] --alias <alias> [--] [command]\n\nFor more information try --help")
                tags.append(args[i+1])
                i+=1
            elif a.startswith("--tag="):
                tags.append(a.split("=",1)[1])
            elif a.startswith("-t="):
                tags.append(a.split("=",1)[1])
            else:
                print_error_and_exit(f"error: Found argument '{a}' which wasn't expected, or isn't valid in this context\n\nUSAGE:\n    {bin_name()} add [FLAGS] [OPTIONS] --alias <alias> [--] [command]\n\nFor more information try --help")
        else:
            if command is None:
                command = a
            else:
                command += " " + a
        i+=1
    if remaining_cmd:
        command = " ".join(remaining_cmd)
    return alias, force, description, tags, command

def handle_add(scripts, default_cfg, config_path, args):
    alias, force, description, tags, command = parse_add_args(args)
    if alias is None:
        print_error_and_exit(f"error: The following required arguments were not provided:\n    --alias <alias>\n\nUSAGE:\n    {bin_name()} add [FLAGS] [OPTIONS] --alias <alias> [--] [command]\n\nFor more information try --help")
    if command is None:
        editor_env = os.environ.get("EDITOR", "")
        editor_display = editor_env
        if not editor_env:
            if "EDITOR" not in os.environ:
                editor_display = "vi"
            else:
                editor_display = editor_env
        if not editor_display:
            error_editor(f"Failed to open `` as a text editor or editor was terminated with errors.")
        try:
            fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix="xvrqt_scrawl_", suffix="_0")
            os.close(fd)
            pathlib.Path(tmp_path).write_text("")
            import shlex
            parts = shlex.split(editor_display)
            if not parts:
                error_editor(f"Failed to open `` as a text editor or editor was terminated with errors.")
            parts.append(tmp_path)
            result = subprocess.run(parts)
            if result.returncode != 0:
                try:
                    os.unlink(tmp_path)
                except:
                    pass
                error_editor(f"Failed to open `{editor_display}` as a text editor or editor was terminated with errors.")
            new_content = pathlib.Path(tmp_path).read_text()
            os.unlink(tmp_path)
            command = new_content
        except FileNotFoundError:
            error_editor(f"Failed to open `{editor_display}` as a text editor or editor was terminated with errors.")
        except Exception:
            error_editor(f"Failed to open `{editor_display}` as a text editor or editor was terminated with errors.")
    if alias in scripts and not force:
        error_alias_exists(alias)
    scripts[alias] = {
        "command": command,
        "description": description,
        "tags": tags if tags else None,
    }
    write_config_file(config_path, scripts, default_cfg)
    print(f"Added {alias}")

def handle_run(scripts, default_cfg, args, verbose):
    for a in args:
        if a == "-h" or a == "--help":
            sys.stdout.write(help_run())
            sys.exit(0)
        if a == "-V" or a == "--version":
            sys.stdout.write(f"{bin_name()}-run 0.1.6\n")
            sys.exit(0)

    alias = None
    script_args = []
    i = 0
    encountered_dd = False
    while i < len(args):
        a = args[i]
        if not encountered_dd and a == "--":
            encountered_dd = True
            i+=1
            continue
        if not encountered_dd and (a == "-h" or a == "--help"):
            sys.stdout.write(help_run())
            sys.exit(0)
        if not encountered_dd and (a == "-V" or a == "--version"):
            sys.stdout.write(f"{bin_name()}-run 0.1.6\n")
            sys.exit(0)
        if not encountered_dd and a.startswith("-") and a != "-":
            print_error_and_exit(f"error: Found argument '{a}' which wasn't expected, or isn't valid in this context\n\nUSAGE:\n    {bin_name()} run <alias> [args]...\n\nFor more information try --help")
        else:
            if alias is None:
                alias = a
            else:
                script_args.append(a)
        i+=1

    if alias is None:
        print_error_and_exit(f"error: The following required arguments were not provided:\n    <alias>\n\nUSAGE:\n    {bin_name()} run <alias> [args]...\n\nFor more information try --help")

    if alias not in scripts:
        error_alias_not_found(alias)

    cmd_str = scripts[alias]["command"]
    if verbose:
        print(f'Starting script "{alias}"', flush=True)
        print("-------------------------", flush=True)
        sys.stdout.flush()
    try:
        sh_cmd = ["sh", "-c", cmd_str, alias] + script_args
        result = subprocess.run(sh_cmd)
        exit_code = result.returncode
    except Exception as e:
        print_error_and_exit(f"error running script: {e}")
        exit_code = 1
    if verbose:
        print("-------------------------", flush=True)
        print("Script complete", flush=True)
    sys.exit(exit_code)

def handle_config_init(cli_config_path):
    target = find_config_path_for_init(cli_config_path)
    parent = target.parent
    if not parent.exists():
        grand = parent.parent
        if not grand.exists():
            error_failed_dir()
        try:
            parent.mkdir(parents=False, exist_ok=False)
        except FileExistsError:
            pass
        except Exception:
            error_failed_dir()
        if not parent.exists():
            error_failed_dir()

    if target.is_file():
        error_cannot_init(str(target))
    try:
        parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    except:
        error_failed_dir()
    if target.is_file():
        error_cannot_init(str(target))
    content = """[scripts.hello-pier]
command = 'echo Hello, Pier!'
description = 'This is an example command.'

[default]
"""
    try:
        target.write_text(content)
    except Exception as e:
        if "No such file" in str(e):
            error_failed_dir()
        print_error_and_exit(f"error: {e}")
    print("Added hello-pier")

def parse_global(args):
    config_path = None
    verbose = False
    verbose_count = 0
    help_flag = None
    version_flag = False
    remaining = []
    i = 0
    encountered_dd = False
    while i < len(args):
        a = args[i]
        if encountered_dd:
            remaining.append(a)
            i+=1
            continue
        if a == "--":
            encountered_dd = True
            i+=1
            continue
        if a == "-h":
            help_flag = "short"
            remaining = args[i+1:]
            break
        elif a == "--help":
            help_flag = "long"
            remaining = args[i+1:]
            break
        elif a == "-V" or a == "--version":
            version_flag = True
            remaining = args[i+1:]
            break
        elif a == "-v" or a == "--verbose":
            verbose_count+=1
            verbose=True
            i+=1
            continue
        elif a == "-c" or a == "--config-file":
            if i+1 >= len(args):
                b = bin_name()
                print_error_and_exit(f"error: The argument '--config-file <path>' requires a value but none was supplied\n\nUSAGE:\n    {b} [FLAGS] [OPTIONS] <alias> [args]...\n    {b} [FLAGS] [OPTIONS] <SUBCOMMAND>\n\nFor more information try --help")
            config_path = args[i+1]
            i+=2
            continue
        elif a.startswith("--config-file="):
            config_path = a.split("=",1)[1]
            i+=1
            continue
        elif a.startswith("-c="):
            config_path = a.split("=",1)[1]
            i+=1
            continue
        elif a.startswith("-c") and len(a)>2:
            config_path = a[2:]
            i+=1
            continue
        elif a.startswith("-") and len(a)>1:
            chars = a[1:]
            if 'h' in chars:
                help_flag = "short"
                remaining = args[i+1:]
                break
            if 'V' in chars:
                version_flag = True
                remaining = args[i+1:]
                break
            j=0
            consumed_next = False
            while j < len(chars):
                ch = chars[j]
                if ch == 'v':
                    verbose_count+=1
                    verbose=True
                elif ch == 'c':
                    rest = chars[j+1:]
                    if rest:
                        if rest.startswith("="):
                            config_path = rest[1:]
                        else:
                            config_path = rest
                        break
                    else:
                        if i+1 >= len(args):
                            b = bin_name()
                            print_error_and_exit(f"error: The argument '--config-file <path>' requires a value but none was supplied\n\nUSAGE:\n    {b} [FLAGS] [OPTIONS] <alias> [args]...\n    {b} [FLAGS] [OPTIONS] <SUBCOMMAND>\n\nFor more information try --help")
                        config_path = args[i+1]
                        consumed_next=True
                        break
                else:
                    print_error_and_exit(f"error: Found argument '{a}' which wasn't expected, or isn't valid in this context\n\nUSAGE:\n    {bin_name()} [FLAGS] [OPTIONS] <alias> [args]...\n    {bin_name()} [FLAGS] [OPTIONS] <SUBCOMMAND>\n\nFor more information try --help")
                j+=1
            i+=1
            if consumed_next:
                i+=1
            continue
        elif a.startswith("-"):
            print_error_and_exit(f"error: Found argument '{a}' which wasn't expected, or isn't valid in this context\n\nUSAGE:\n    {bin_name()} [FLAGS] [OPTIONS] <alias> [args]...\n    {bin_name()} [FLAGS] [OPTIONS] <SUBCOMMAND>\n\nFor more information try --help")
        else:
            remaining.append(a)
            remaining.extend(args[i+1:])
            break
        i+=1

    return config_path, verbose, verbose_count, help_flag, version_flag, remaining, encountered_dd
